author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Police detained a driver Friday evening after reports that a motorist displayed what appeared to be a gun during a road-rage incident in Halifax, Massachusetts. Officers in neighboring Kingston later located a vehicle matching the description and stopped it near a restaurant on Main Street, also known as Route 3.

Kingston police said the driver was argumentative and initially resisted commands, but officers took the person into custody without further incident. A search of the vehicle turned up a realistic-looking pellet gun. According to police, the driver said the object had only been shown to someone else.

The detained driver was transferred to Halifax police, which is handling the underlying investigation. Authorities had not released the person’s name or announced charges when the incident was reported. The case illustrates the difficulty officers face when replica or pellet guns are reported in public: responders generally must treat the object as a potentially lethal weapon until it can be safely recovered and identified. Police did not report any injuries connected to the stop.
dek: Kingston officers stopped the vehicle described by witnesses and recovered a pellet gun that police said looked realistic.
headline: Police detain road-rage suspect after realistic pellet gun found
